question: Should signed publisher-feed traversal and its trust-root configuration become an OpenClaw core capability now, or remain outside core until an owner plugin and production consumer are defined?
rationale: The branch creates a reusable security-sensitive transport primitive but does not establish the product owner, persisted/configured trust source, or runtime lifecycle that should invoke it; repository policy requires those boundaries to be deliberate.

options.title: Pause for owner design
options.body: Keep this foundation unmerged until maintainers choose the core or plugin owner, trust-root source, and supported production entry point.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded core slice
options.body: Approve a named core owner and require this branch to add the corresponding runtime caller, upgrade/configuration contract, and live signed-endpoint proof before merge.

options.title: Move the consumer outward
options.body: Keep generic seams only if needed and implement publisher-feed behavior in an owner plugin or ClawHub package once the existing extension contracts are confirmed sufficient.

recommendation.title: Pause for owner design
recommendation.body: Keep this foundation unmerged until maintainers choose the core or plugin owner, trust-root source, and supported production entry point.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked proposal stack and can supply the intended consumer and protocol boundary, while maintainers retain the product decision.
